commands.name: context
commands.summary: What flk sees right now: host health, the current app, machines, ports, next steps

options.description: Every app on this host, not just the current one
Print JSON
Skip the host checks (flk doctor): cheap enough to poll; host is just lan_ip

notes: Run this first. It resolves the app the same way other commands do (-a APP, or flk.toml / fly.toml in the current directory) and works even when there is none.
Also tidies machines that exited on their own, like status does.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: Show help for flk, a command, or a topic (cheatsheet, install, first-app, operate, troubleshoot, uninstall)

options.description: The full reference: concepts, every command, config, workflows, gotchas
With --all: the command table as JSON

notes: `flk COMMAND --help` is the same as `flk help COMMAND`.

commands.name: completion
commands.summary: Print a tab-completion script (bash; zsh via bashcompinit)
notes: Install: echo 'source <(flk completion bash)' >> ~/.bashrc  (or, with bash-completion loaded: flk completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/flk)
zsh: autoload -U bashcompinit && bashcompinit && source <(flk completion bash)

commands.name: setup
commands.summary: Download firecracker + guest kernel (no root), then run doctor
notes: Root setup (bridge, taps, NAT, port helper) is separate: sudo /home/dayne/flk/setup-host.sh

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check host readiness

options.description: Print JSON instead of a table

notes: --json prints {"schema", "ok", "checks": [{"label", "status", "hint"}], "services": [...]}; status is pass, fail or warn. warn means flk works but an optional feature (port forwarding) is off; ok is false only when a check fails.
services: flk-net.service and flk-machines.service as systemd sees them: {"unit", "installed", "enabled", "active", "sub", "result", "since"}.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Print the flk version

commands.name: resume
commands.summary: Start every machine that should be running (after a reboot, or after stop-all)
notes: Should be running: started, restarted, deployed or scaled, and not stopped with `flk machine stop` since. A machine whose app exited counts too.
flk-machines.service runs it at boot (sudo /home/dayne/flk/setup-host.sh --install-service).
-a APP limits it to one app.

commands.name: stop-all
commands.summary: Gracefully stop every running machine, remembering to resume them
notes: What the host does at shutdown (flk-machines.service): all machines stop in parallel, each with its kill_timeout, and `flk resume` brings them back.
To stop a machine for good, use `flk machine stop`.
-a APP limits it to one app.

commands.name: launch
commands.usage: flk launch [--name NAME] [--image IMAGE] [--port PORT] [--cpus N] [--memory MB] [--no-deploy]
commands.summary: Create flk.toml (if missing) in the current directory, register the app, deploy

options.description: App name (default: directory name)
Use a prebuilt image instead of a Dockerfile
internal_port in the generated flk.toml (default 8080)
vCPUs in the generated flk.toml (default 1)
Memory in the generated flk.toml (default 256)
Register the app but don't deploy

notes: An existing flk.toml or fly.toml is used as-is; the options only shape a new one.
Deploys right away unless --no-deploy, or there's no Dockerfile / [build] image yet.

commands.name: deploy
commands.summary: Build the image and roll machines to a new release

options.description: Deploy this image instead of building

notes: Reads flk.toml / fly.toml in the current directory, or with -a APP the file flk recorded at the app's last launch/deploy, so it works from anywhere.
Creates machines on the first deploy (count from `flk scale count`, default 1); later deploys stop, update and reboot each machine in turn.
Waits up to 30s per machine for internal_port to accept connections, then warns but carries on.
Volumes named in [[mounts]] must exist first: flk volumes create NAME --size 1 (one per machine).

commands.name: logs
commands.summary: Serial console output (app stdout/stderr and boot messages)

options.description: One machine (default: all)
Lines of history (default 50)
Keep following, even without a terminal
Print and exit, even in a terminal

notes: Follows new output only when stdout is a terminal; piped or run by an agent it prints the last lines and exits.
Each machine keeps console.log, rotated to console.log.1 past FLK_LOG_MAX_MB (default 10) MB.

commands.name: console
commands.summary: Attach to a machine's serial console, or --send one line to the app's stdin

options.description: Type one line into the app's stdin, then return (no terminal needed)
With --send: print console output until a line matches REGEX
With --wait-log: give up after this long (default 10)

commands.blocks: attaches an interactive terminal; agents: use --send (and --wait-log), or `flk logs`
notes: Detach with Ctrl-b d (Ctrl-b Ctrl-b d inside tmux). Attaching needs a terminal; --send doesn't.

--send types TEXT and Enter into the app's stdin (needs [flk] stdin = "console", the default). With --wait-log it then prints the console output until a line matches REGEX (exit 1 after --timeout). The console echoes what you type; that echo is skipped when matching.
It's the serial console, not a shell: you see app output and type to its stdin (server consoles: stop, say, op...). Ctrl-C here doesn't signal the app; use flk machine stop.
`flk ssh console` is an alias.

commands.summary: Alias: `flk ssh console` = `flk console`

subcommands.summary: Volumes and what they're attached to

options.description: Print JSON instead of a table

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.usage: flk volumes create NAME [--size GB] [--path FILE] [--from-dir DIR]
subcommands.summary: Create a volume for [[mounts]] source = NAME

options.description: Size in GB (default 1)
Create the image at FILE (e.g. on a bigger disk) instead of flk's state dir; flk never deletes it
Fill it with a copy of DIR (owner/group IDs kept as-is)

subcommands.name: import
subcommands.summary: Register an existing ext4 image as a volume; flk never deletes it

options.description: An existing ext4 image file (required)

notes: Size comes from the file. Don't mount it on the host while a machine uses it.

subcommands.name: destroy
subcommands.summary: Delete an unattached volume and its data (external volumes: unregister, keep the file)

options.description: Also delete an external (--path / import) volume's file

subcommands.name: backup
subcommands.usage: flk volumes backup [ID|NAME...] [--to DIR] [--keep N] [--mode MODE] [--no-check]
subcommands.summary: Copy volumes (default: all of the app's) to the backup dir, then prune old copies

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Keep this many backups per volume (default: [flk.backup] keep, host backup_keep, 7)
stop, live or pause: override [flk.backup] mode
Skip the e2fsck of the copy

notes: How the app is kept from writing comes from [flk.backup] in flk.toml (see flk help --all): by default its machine is stopped for the copy and started again; mode = "live" with pre/post hooks (e.g. save-off / save-on) copies while it runs.
Copies are sparse, and instant on XFS/btrfs when the backup dir shares the volume's filesystem. The copy is checked with e2fsck (a copy of a running machine gets its journal replayed).

subcommands.name: backups
subcommands.summary: List a volume's backups (default: all of the app's volumes), newest first

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Print JSON instead of a table

subcommands.name: restore
subcommands.summary: Replace a volume's data with a backup (default: the latest); its machine must be stopped

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)

notes: BACKUP is a file name from flk volumes backups, or part of it (e.g. its date). The current image is kept beside it as FILE.before-restore-TIME, not deleted.

subcommands.name: extend
subcommands.summary: Grow a volume and its filesystem; its machine must be stopped

options.description: New size in GB (required; grow only)
